Originally published at recca0120.github.io
You open analytics.google.com in Chrome and click the certificate — and see this:
Subject: filament-scu.test
Issuer: Laravel Valet CA Self Signed CN

That's not Google's certificate. That's your local Laravel Valet CA leaking onto an external site.
This isn't a browser bug or a Google problem — it's your local dev environment intercepting traffic it shouldn't.
Valet builds a local dev stack out of three components:
dnsmasq: resolves *.test domains to 127.0.0.1


nginx: listens on 127.0.0.1, routes requests to local sites by server_name


Valet CA: signs HTTPS certificates for each .test site
In a correct setup, /etc/resolver/test scopes only *.test lookups to dnsmasq; external domains go through the system DNS. The two never cross paths.
But ther…

articles.author: Henry Godnick
articles.description:
A lot of AI cost advice starts too late.
It tells you to review the bill after the damage is done.
That never worked for me.
The real problem is not that AI is expensive. The problem is that the expensive part happens quietly. One more prompt. One more rewrite. One more huge context dump. Then you look up later and realize you spent money on a conversation that had stopped being useful.
That is why I built TokenBar.
TokenBar is a macOS menu bar app that keeps token usage and spend visible while I am actually working. Not in a dashboard. Not in a tab I will check later. Right there in the menu bar, where the number can bother me before the bill does.
That tiny shift changed how I use AI:
I notice runaway loops faster
I stop pretending giant context windows are free
I choose cheaper models when the task does not need the expensive one
I catch waste while I can still do something about it
I did not build TokenBar because I wanted another chart.
If you are shipping with Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, or any other metered tool, the most useful thing you can do is make the cost visible while you work.
That is the whole product.
articles.title: Why I Built TokenBar: AI Spend Should Not Be a Monthly Surprise
